description: Unify two generations of a purchase events table into one consistent result. purchases_v1 stores user_id as INT64, the event time as epoch SECONDS (INT64) and the amount in integer cents, always in USD. purchases_v2 stores user_id as STRING, the event time as TIMESTAMP, the amount as a decimal in major units, plus a currency column. During the migration both systems were written in parallel, so the same event_uuid can exist in both tables; in that case keep only the v2 row. Output columns: event_uuid (STRING), user_id (INT64), event_ts (TIMESTAMP), amount (FLOAT64, major units), currency (STRING), source_version (STRING: 'v1' or 'v2'). Sort by event_ts.

user_id.description: User identifier serialized as a string

edge_cases: Event 'b' exists in both tables and must appear once, from v2
v1 amounts are cents and must be divided by 100; v2 amounts are already major units
v1 timestamps are epoch seconds (not milliseconds)
v2 user_id strings that are not numeric must become NULL rather than failing the query
common_failure_modes: FM5: UNION ALL matches columns by position, so differing column order/types silently mixes cents with dollars or fails on type mismatch
FM4: TIMESTAMP_MILLIS instead of TIMESTAMP_SECONDS places v1 events in January 1970
FM3: UNION ALL without deduplicating on event_uuid double-counts dual-written events (UNION DISTINCT does not help because the rows differ)
